headline: Markets pause and reposition ahead of Nvidia and Jackson Hole
body: Futures are mixed and largely directionless this morning, a pause after last week's broader risk-off pullback that left the S&P 500 down roughly 1.4% and the Nasdaq closer to 2% as investors reassessed stretched tech valuations -- the sector's forward P/E sits near 30x versus a 22x ten-year average. The tone reads as wait-and-see rather than fearful: positioning ahead of two major catalysts rather than a retreat from risk outright. Wednesday brings Nvidia's earnings, treated as a referendum on whether AI infrastructure spending can keep justifying mega-cap multiples, and Friday brings new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first Jackson Hole keynote, the most closely parsed speech of the week. A breakdown in US-Canada trade talks and fresh sanctions threats tied to Iran add a layer of geopolitical unease on top of the valuation debate.

The more telling signal may be underneath equities. Gold has pushed to a three-month high near $4,640 on roughly a 15% rally this month, and the dollar is trading near multi-month lows, after the Treasury's surprise move to expand buybacks of long-dated debt reignited fiscal-sustainability and 'debasement trade' concerns even as it pulled yields lower. Weak July payrolls and retail-sales data have leaned market expectations toward a Fed that stays on hold through year-end, with easing bets pushed into 2027. Retail chatter on WallStreetBets tracks the same names driving the institutional story -- Nvidia and Amazon dominate mention volume, alongside a sharp jump in Palantir mentions -- suggesting retail positioning is following the AI-earnings narrative rather than diverging from it.
